answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The umber multiplier is published, charged in sable, and horizon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 2394 identities would post 3039 proofs and burn roughly 45 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
